items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated.
judge.evidence_topic: The Continued Influence Effect (CIE) is the phenomenon that retracted information often continues to influence judgments and inferences.
judge.reason: O resumo relata que o CIE também aparece quando a credibilidade é igual (Experiment 2), o que não é mencionado no achado extraído. O achado é parcialmente sustentado.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (CIE), utiliza dois experimentos com participantes humanos e materiais neutros (relatos de eventos fictícios com retratação). O resumo afirma que uma fronteira de evento reduziu o CIE no Experimento 2, corroborando integralmente o achado extraído.

items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo é sobre continued influence effect, o resumo menciona experimentos e a extração do achado principal é apoiada diretamente pelo trecho 'we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness'.

items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The results show that the reliability of corrections’ sources did not affect their processing when participants were not inoculated.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE) is a phenomenon in which certain information, although retracted and corrected, still has an impact on event reporting, reasoning, inference, and decisions.
judge.reason: O resumo menciona explicitamente o efeito de influência continuada da desinformação (CIE) e investiga a redução desse efeito, atendendo ao tema. O estudo é empírico com participantes humanos, como indicado pela menção a 'participants' e manipulação experimental. O método extraído descreve 'Seis cenários narrativos fictícios', o que não é suportado pelo resumo, que não especifica o número ou o tipo de cenários. O achado diz que a inoculação reduziu a dependência da desinformação e que a credibilidade da fonte só importou para os inoculados, mas o resumo mostra que a redução só ocorreu com fonte de alta credibilidade (condicional), e também relata que a crença na desinformação, não na retratação, previu a dependência, tornando o achado parcialmente suportado.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_topic: The term “continued influence effect” (CIE) refers to the phenomenon that discredited and obsolete information continues to affect behavior and beliefs. [...] we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors [...] to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.reason: O estudo investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada da desinformação, usando experimentos com cenários fictícios neutros (acidente de micro-ônibus, arrombamento, incêndio), sem conteúdo político ou de saúde. Os dados extraídos são compatíveis com o resumo.

items.title: The role of discomfort in the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Studies 1 and 2 found that retractions of misinformation elicit psychological discomfort, and this discomfort predicts continued belief in and use of misinformation.
judge.evidence_topic: Research examining the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has reliably found that belief in misinformation persists even after the misinformation has been retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada da informação falsa (CIE); relata três estudos experimentais com dados próprios; o resumo menciona retratações e medidas de desconforto, crença e uso, compatível com o método extraído; o achado principal é uma paráfrase exata do que o resumo afirma.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: through three experiments. Experiment 1 explored the general impact... Experiment 2 further dissected... Experiment 3 delved into the mechanisms
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction. This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada com experimentos, atendendo ao tema e ao critério empírico. Contudo, o resumo não descreve os materiais (incêndios) mencionados no método extraído, de modo que esse detalhe não pode ser confirmado. O achado está plenamente respaldado pelo resumo. O tamanho da amostra, não informado no resumo, está correto.

items.title: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions
judge.evidence_topic: Retracted misinformation often continues to influence event-related reasoning, but there is mixed evidence that it influences person impressions. Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.reason: O estudo trata do continued influence effect com materiais neutros (pessoa fictícia, comportamento negativo retratado). O resumo descreve três experimentos com participantes humanos, e o método extraído reflete exatamente o paradigma descrito: formação de impressão com retratação. O achado extraído ('A influência contínua da afirmação retratada apareceu em apenas um dos três experimentos, nos outros dois ela foi totalmente descartada.') é corroborado literalmente pelo resumo: 'Evidence for the continued influence of the retracted behaviour statement was found in one experiment; in the other two experiments the retracted misinformation was fully discounted.'

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e atende ao recorte temático (trecho: "Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE)"). É um estudo empírico com participantes humanos, que completaram medidas de funções executivas e uma tarefa de CIE (trecho: "Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents... and a standard CIE task"). O método extraído inclui "oito relatos de eventos, metade retratada", detalhe não presente no resumo, que menciona apenas "a standard CIE task". Assim, o método informado não confere integralmente com o resumo (method_ok = false). O achado principal ("As funções executivas predizem a suscetibilidade ao CIE, em especial a atualização da memória de trabalho") é plenamente sustentado pelo resumo: "Results showed that EF can predict susceptibility to the CIE, especially the factor of working-memory updating".

items.title: Effective mitigation of the belief perseverance bias after the retraction of misinformation: Awareness training and counter-speech

judge.evidence_empirical: in an experiment with N = 251 participants
judge.evidence_topic: Research has shown that individuals persevere in their biased beliefs and opinions even after the retraction of misinformation. This phenomenon is known as the belief perseverance bias.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do belief perseverance bias, conceito análogo ao continued influence effect, e o resumo confirma ser um experimento com N=251 que mede opiniões após retratação, usando técnicas de desassociação. O método extraído está em conformidade com o resumo (experimento comparando três técnicas, medições repetidas), e o achado principal é apoiado pela declaração de que a CS é a mais eficaz com tamanho de efeito grande.

items.title: Combating false information in military situations: Striking the right balance between continued influence effect and overcorrection

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making, followed by an assessment of their inferential reasoning.
judge.evidence_topic: while others highlight the continued influence effect (CIE), where attitudes persist in alignment with FI.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga diretamente o continued influence effect e efeitos de correção, utilizando experimento com participantes humanos que mede raciocínio inferencial após retratação. O achado extraído corresponde exatamente ao relato do resumo.

items.title: Reading Medium and Epistemic Emotions in the Continued Influence Effect of Misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: This was a within-subjects experiment in that two events were read on paper and two on screen to compare effects of reading medium.
judge.evidence_topic: It is well known that misinformation’s effects on memory linger, referred to as the continued influence effect, even after reading corrections. However, it is uncertain how the reading medium and epistemic emotions (relevant to knowledge construction) relate to the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o continued influence effect com um experimento intrassujeitos usando notícias fictícias e correções, medindo crença após a correção. O achado extraído é suportado pelo resumo.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted. Person impressions were recorded after the presentation of each behaviour description.
judge.evidence_topic: Despite robust evidence that misinformation continues to influence event-related reasoning after a clear retraction, evidence for the continued influence of misinformation on person impressions is mixed. Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada da desinformação em impressões sobre pessoas após retratação, utilizando cenário fictício neutro (protagonista "John"). O resumo relata quatro experimentos com coleta de dados próprios, e o achado extraído — de que a desinformação foi eficazmente descartada após retratação clara — é exatamente sustentado pelo trecho 'participants fully discounted the misinformation once retracted' e pela conclusão de que 'person-related misinformation can be effectively discounted following a clear retraction'.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323). We observed the CIE in all conditions
judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later. Participants typically continue to refer to the corrected misinformation when making inferential statements about the event.
judge.reason: O artigo relata experimentos online medindo o efeito de influência continuada com um cenário fictício neutro (incêndio em armazém), sem conotação política ou de saúde, com dados próprios; os dados extraídos refletem corretamente o resumo.

items.title: The independent effects of source expertise and trustworthiness on retraction believability: The moderating role of vested interest

judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source while controlling for perceptions of trustworthiness. Additionally, Study 1 demonstrated that this only occurs when the source had no vested interest in issuing the retraction. Study 2 found similar effects using a design containing manipulations of both expertise and trustworthiness.
judge.evidence_topic: retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source
judge.reason: O artigo investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada (crença após retratação) com cenário fictício neutro (incêndio em armazém) e experimentos com participantes humanos. O resumo confirma que retratações de fonte especialista reduzem a crença continuada, alinhando-se exatamente ao achado extraído.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O artigo trata diretamente do efeito de influência continuada usando experimentos com cenários fictícios neutros, atende ao recorte de estudos empíricos com dados próprios e os dados extraídos condizem com o resumo.

items.title: Enhancing misinformation correction: New variants and a combination of awareness training and counter-speech to mitigate belief perseverance bias

judge.evidence_empirical: an experiment involving N = 876 individuals
judge.evidence_topic: Belief perseverance bias refers to individuals' tendency to persevere in biased opinions even after the misinformation that initially shaped those opinions has been retracted.
judge.reason: The article clearly addresses the continued influence effect (belief perseverance after retraction), is an experiment with human participants measuring belief, the materials are presented as neutral (real-life issue and no indication of political or health topics), the study type and method description match the abstract, and the main finding is directly supported by the abstract statement that the combination was more effective than single techniques.

items.title: The neural basis of the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Thirty-one participants (10 males) were recruited in this study. They were instructed to read brief, fictional news reports and answer three inference questions after reading while lying in a 3.0T Siemens Prisma MRI scanner.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often continues to influence people’s beliefs and reasoning even after retracted—this persistence is termed the ‘continued influence effect of misinformation’ (CIEM).
judge.reason: O resumo não relata comparação de pontuações de inferência, apenas resultados neurais; o achado extraído afirma que as pontuações foram maiores na condição com retratação, o que não é sustentado.

items.title: Working memory capacity, short-term memory capacity, and the continued influence effect: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants (N=216) completed a continued-influence task, as well as a battery of WM and STM capacity tasks.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often affects inferences and judgments even after it has been retracted and discredited. This is known as the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do Efeito de Influência Continuada, realiza experimento com participantes humanos, os dados extraídos estão em conformidade com o resumo e o achado principal encontra suporte literal no resumo.

items.title: Electrophysiological correlates of the continued influence effect of misinformation: an exploratory study

judge.evidence_empirical: We present the first investigation into the CIE using event-related potentials (ERPs). Participants completed a continued-influence task whilst electroencephalographic data were recorded.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often affects inferential reasoning even after it has been retracted, known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada com um experimento usando EEG, conforme solicitado, e o achado extraído está alinhado com o resumo.

items.title: Cause typicality and the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: In three experiments, we interrogated the importance of cause typicality for the generalizable utility of these correction strategies by manipulating the typicality of initial and alternative causes.
judge.evidence_topic: A large body of research has focused on whether and how readers update their knowledge of events when an initial piece of causal information is corrected. These studies have indicated that corrections can reduce, but do not eliminate, readers' reliance on the initial cause when drawing inferences or making decisions about the events (i.e., the continued influence effect).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada usando experimentos com participantes humanos, manipulando a tipicidade da causa inicial e medindo a dependência antes e depois da correção. O resumo menciona explicitamente o continued influence effect e os achados extraídos são plenamente sustentados.

items.title: How do forewarnings and post-warnings affect misinformation reliance? The impact of warnings on the continued influence effect and belief regression

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments (N = 337), we found that while a forewarning did reduce reliance on misinformation, retrospectively warned participants (when the warning was placed either between the misinformation and the retraction or just before testing) relied on the misinformation to a similar degree as unwarned participants.
judge.evidence_topic: People often continue to rely on certain information in their reasoning, even if this information has been retracted; this is called the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) em um experimento com humanos, sem menção a temas polticos ou de sade, e os dados extrados conferem precisamento com o resumo.

items.title: Do the protective effects last? The effectiveness of alternative + forewarning/inoculation techniques in reducing misinformation reliance and reliance regression in the continued influence effect procedure

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments (N = 441)
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) refers to continued reliance on misinformation, even after it has been retracted.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de influência continuada da desinformação, apresenta dois experimentos com participantes humanos (N=441), o método descrito corresponde ao resumo, e o achado principal encontra respaldo no trecho que indica que o efeito protetor das técnicas combinadas não se sustentou, com aumento da dependência da desinformação ao longo do tempo.

items.title: Does evaluating belief prior to its retraction influence the efficacy of later corrections?

judge.evidence_empirical: In the current study, participants evaluated their belief in the target cause by either rating how much they believed it caused the outcome (Experiment 1) or rating the probability that the target caused the outcome (Experiment 2).
judge.evidence_topic: assessing whether rating the strength of one’s belief in the initially reported, mistaken cause might influence the efficacy of a later correction.
judge.reason: O achado principal extraído coincide diretamente com o resultado relatado no resumo: "The results showed that evaluating belief in a target cause prior to its retraction (relative to not doing so) rendered the correction more effective."

items.title: I know It's false, but I keep thinking as if it were true: A replication study of Johnson and Seifert's (1994) continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.evidence_topic: Researchers Johnson and Seifert (1994, Experiment 1A) penned a seminal paper on this 'Continued Influence Effect' (CIE), which they observed in English-speaking participants. In their experiments, one group read a text containing FI that was later retracted (FI group), while another read the same text without FI (control group).
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que os resultados confirmam os do estudo original, que demonstrou o efeito de influência continuada. Isso sustenta integralmente o achado extraído: 'A replicação confirmou o resultado do estudo original: a informação falsa retratada continuou influenciando o raciocínio'.
